pages.summary: Original lesson 'LinearOpMode to command-based' (SolversLib 0.3.6, FTC SDK 12.0). It follows the FRC time-based-to-command-based page section by section. Sections: intro (links the FRC page and its own names table); Versions note; 'Who runs the loop' (a simplified CommandOpMode.runOpMode() lifecycle, run() = CommandScheduler.getInstance().run(), the scheduler's four steps taken from the 0.3.6 source, no fixed 20 ms); 'The three pieces' table and the two rules; 'The simplest example' (a LinearOpMode code window; 'Add SolversLib to your project' with the TeamCode/build.gradle lines or the SolversLib Quickstart; a command-based code window with subsystems/Intake.java (SubsystemBase, hardwareMap in the constructor, runIn()/stop() via run()) and IntakeTeleOp.java (CommandOpMode, initialize(), setDefaultCommand, GamepadEx(gamepad1).getGamepadButton(GamepadKeys.Button.A).whenHeld(...)); a warning to create subsystems in initialize(); a collapsible import list that warns about the command.old package); 'Pressing A, loop by loop', traced from the CommandScheduler/Trigger source (the default command starts at the end of loop 1 and runs from loop 2; on release, stop() starts at the end of loop 9 and runs from loop 10, so the motor keeps its last power for one loop), plus a 'whenHeld or whileHeld?' note showing the difference with withTimeout; 'Inside a command' (initialize/execute/isFinished/end table, then runOnce, startEnd, withTimeout(ms), andThen, Commands.sequence/parallel/waitMillis, and the fact that a group holds every requirement its commands use); 'What's different on FTC' (comparison table plus subsections: one OpMode is one program and reset(); INIT vs PLAY with initialize_loop() and an @Autonomous example scheduled in preRun(), explaining why not initialize(); telemetry via a run() override with super.run(); bulk reads via CommandScheduler.getInstance().setBulkReading(hardwareMap, BulkCachingMode.AUTO), handing off to Mechanism control); a WPILib-to-SolversLib names table; 'Other frameworks you'll see' (FTCLib, NextFTC v1/v2, Ivy, one paragraph each, no docs.ftclib.org link); 'Try it' (a Claw subsystem with runOnce open/close on the bumpers via whenPressed, and a sequential auto in preRun(), with a 'You're done when...' checkpoint); Every external link returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-10.

Things other pages should know:
(1) The bindings are whenHeld (= WPILib whileTrue), whenPressed, whenReleased and toggleWhenPressed. Trigger has whenActive and whileActiveOnce. SolversLib has no until(); its equivalent is interruptOn(BooleanSupplier).
(2) withTimeout(long millis) and Commands.waitMillis(long) take milliseconds.
(3) Commands.parallel throws if two of its commands require the same subsystem.
(4) setDefaultCommand throws if the command doesn't require that subsystem or if it is already finished.
(5) CommandScheduler.setBulkReading(hardwareMap, mode) exists. With MANUAL, the scheduler clears every hub's cache at the end of each run(), but not during INIT. The page recommends AUTO and hands MANUAL off to mechanism-control.md.
(6) The SolversLib source has a com.seattlesolvers.solverslib.command.old package that duplicates some class names. Alt+Enter can pick the wrong one, so the page warns about it.
(7) The build.gradle lines are a plain groovy block, not part of the code window, because the window CSS gives every file a Java 'J' icon.

Cross-links go to first-opmode.md, first-autonomous.md, mechanism-control.md, path-following.md and the FRC page, all at page level. The only anchor link is #wpilib-to-solverslib-names, on this page.

remaining_doubts.doubt: None of the Java samples were compiled. I checked every SolversLib call against the 0.3.6 git-tag sources: CommandOpMode, CommandScheduler, Subsystem, SubsystemBase, Command, Commands, Button, Trigger, GamepadButton, GamepadEx, GamepadKeys, RunCommand, InstantCommand, StartEndCommand, WaitCommand, Timing.Timer, ParallelRaceGroup, ParallelCommandGroup, SequentialCommandGroup and CommandGroupBase. I checked the SDK calls against the RobotCore 12.0.0 javadoc: opModeInInit, DcMotorSimple.getPower/setPower, and Gamepad bumpers. The loop-by-loop trace and the whenHeld/whileHeld-with-withTimeout note match the scheduler and Trigger code. Nothing was run on a robot.

The claim that SolversLib 'doesn't work in OnBot Java' matches the index page and the outline. However, OnBot Java has an external-library upload feature, and I didn't verify that SolversLib (with its kotlin-stdlib and ejml dependencies) can't be loaded that way. The claim is probably true in practice but wasn't proven.

The page recommends BulkCachingMode.AUTO and leaves MANUAL to mechanism-control.md. SolversLib's own javadoc on setBulkReading calls MANUAL 'highly recommended', because the scheduler clears every hub's cache at the end of each run(). If mechanism-control.md teaches MANUAL with a hand-written clearBulkCache() every loop, students using CommandScheduler.setBulkReading(MANUAL) would clear the cache twice. That page should mention it. mechanism-control.md is still a placeholder, so I couldn't check the hand-off.

These details come from standard Android Studio and FTC behaviour, not from a fetched source: 'Sync Now', the advice to refuse AGP upgrade/downgrade prompts (from the outline), keeping auto-to-teleop data in a static field, and robotPeriodic running while disabled. I did verify the WPILib binding and composition names (onTrue/onFalse/whileTrue/toggleOnTrue, until, withTimeout in seconds, Commands.waitSeconds/sequence/parallel/race) on docs.wpilib.org.

The Gradle snippet goes in TeamCode/build.gradle and uses `url = "..."`, following the SolversLib docs and the Quickstart. The outline instead said build.dependencies.gradle and `url "..."`. I kept the writer's choice because it matches the primary sources, and Gradle 9 deprecates the space-assignment form. Other pages' install lines should use the same form.

pages.summary:
An original lesson with a curated reading list. It covers:
- The spin vs position split, with a table and a link to team 2910's roller/servo section.
- The built-in RunModes table, with the correct motor type in the configuration.
- `DcMotorEx.setVelocity` (ticks/s) for a flywheel.
- RUN_TO_POSITION call order (target, then mode, then unsigned power), and that it holds position.
- Why teams write their own loops: 20 Hz (gm0), a P-only position stage, no gravity term.
- Feedback vs feedforward, with tables for P/D/I and kG/kCos/kS.

The main code window is a SolversLib `Lift extends SubsystemBase` whose constructor takes `HardwareMap`. Its `periodic()` reads the encoder once, then does P + D + kG with `ElapsedTime` dt and `Range.clip`. `goTo(ticks)` is `runOnce(target = ticks).andThen(Commands.waitUntil(this::atTarget))`. `LiftTeleOp` (a CommandOpMode) turns on `setBulkReading(AUTO)`, binds Y/A with `whenPressed`, and shows loop-time telemetry. A collapsible lists the imports.

The rest of the page:
- A direction-check warning.
- A 'Pressing Y, loop by loop' walkthrough.
- A tuning order (kG, then kP, then kD, then an optional clamped I).
- An arm kCos snippet and a tip on SolversLib's PIDFController.
- Bulk reads: an OFF/AUTO/MANUAL table, the plain SDK loop, and the SolversLib one-liner (in MANUAL it clears the cache itself). Also notes that I2C devices aren't bulk-read, plus the ConceptMotorBulkRead link.
- Live tuning with Panels `@Configurable` or FTC Dashboard `@Config`, including the copy trap for HIGH/LOW, linked to tools.md.
- The CTRL ALT FTC chapter list in order, with a Credit admonition (no stated license, link only).
- Try it: tune the lift, then add MID and a nudge. Checkpoint, then Learn more.

pages.summary:
An original lesson with curated links. A Versions note warns about the SDK 12 AprilTag break.

**IMU:** BHI260AP (Control Hubs from September 2022) vs BNO055; the universal IMU interface is the only way to use the BHI260AP; Expansion Hubs bought after December 2021 have no IMU; the default name is "imu". pages.summary: Your first OpMode, an original lesson. It covers what an OpMode is: the @TeleOp/@Autonomous annotation (name, group, @Disabled) and the INIT/PLAY/STOP table, with a note that FTC Docs calls the PLAY button Start and the Javadoc calls it play. A code window holds IntakeLinear.java: a LinearOpMode that runs the "intake" motor at 0.8 while A is held, sends telemetry with update(), and has a vscode__note. Then a step-by-step 'INIT, PLAY and STOP' walkthrough and four rules: get hardware inside runOpMode, names must match the configuration and are case-sensitive, call telemetry.update(), check opModeIsActive(). A gamepad input table covers the left_stick_y sign, triggers 0 to 1, left_trigger_pressed and the PlayStation button aliases. Edge detection shows aWasPressed()/aWasReleased() with a loop-by-loop table, a warning about the consume-once trap (wrong and right code), and a collapsible on the older Gamepad.copy() pattern. A motor method table covers setPower, setDirection and ZeroPowerBehavior BRAKE/FLOAT. Servos cover Servo.setPosition 0 to 1 (getPosition returns the last command) and CRServo.setPower. The iterative OpMode section has an init/init_loop/start/loop/stop table and a two-file code window (IntakeIterative.java plus IntakeLinear.java to compare), the 'telemetry is automatic' and 'never wait in loop()' rules, and a LinearOpMode vs OpMode comparison table with which style the course uses when (CommandOpMode is a LinearOpMode). 'Try it' asks for an A toggle with aWasPressed and a claw servo on the bumpers (same names as linear-to-command-based's Claw exercise), with a 'You're done when' checkpoint. Learn more links FTC Docs, gm0, the SDK samples and the 12.0.0 Javadoc. One TODO diagram comment. Collapsible import lists sit under each window for OnBot Java users.
uncertain: 'Your code stops, and the motors turn off' at STOP: there is no official SDK statement. A FIRST forum answer says motors 'release' after STOP, and I worded it to match that.
The exact error text when a hardwareMap name is wrong is not quoted. The page only says the OpMode stops with an error saying it can't find the device.
That the Driver Station shows @Autonomous OpModes in a separate Autonomous list: FTC Docs only describes the TeleOp list, and the Autonomous list is from general knowledge.
'The robot shouldn't drive yet' during INIT is stated as good practice, not as a game-manual rule.

pages.summary: Mecanum drive, an original lesson. Versions note (SDK 12.0, front_left_drive etc. since 10.3, universal IMU). It explains how mecanum wheels move, with a table for forward, strafe right and turn right, the X roller pattern, and why strafing is slower (gm0). Robot-centric: gm0's math (y = -left_stick_y, x * 1.1, rx; denominator = max(|y|+|x|+|rx|, 1)), with a worked example of why clipping breaks the power ratio. Wide code window MecanumTeleOp.java with a vscode__note. 'Test the motor directions first' explains that the SDK samples reverse the left side and gm0 reverses the right. The test uses BasicOmniOpMode_Linear's X/A/Y/B one-wheel trick to check names and directions, then forward-stick and strafe checks. Field-centric: IMU facts (BHI260AP from September 2022, BNO055 before, Expansion Hubs after December 2021 have none), RevHubOrientationOnRobot logo/USB directions with impossible pairs rejected, and getRobotYawPitchRollAngles().getYaw(AngleUnit.RADIANS). Yaw runs -180 to 180 and goes up when the robot turns left. resetYaw only when flat. Heading persists between OpModes (FTC Docs). Reset on options (start on Xbox). The rotate-by-minus-heading math has a worked 90-degree example. Wide two-file code window: FieldCentricTeleOp.java uses a while(opModeInInit()) heading readout like RobotAutoDriveByGyro_Linear, and MecanumTeleOp.java is there to compare. An IMU check procedure and a note that RobotTeleopMecanumFieldRelativeDrive's atan2/hypot method is equivalent. 'Try it' covers slow mode on the right bumper and robot-centric on the left bumper, with a checkpoint. Learn more links gm0 Mecanum TeleOp and Holonomic Drivetrains, FTC Docs IMU, the two SDK samples and sensors-and-vision.md. Two TODO diagram comments.
uncertain: 'A motor with no setDirection line runs FORWARD' (the default direction) comes from SDK convention. The Javadoc pages I read don't state it.
'Some pairs are impossible ... the OpMode stops with an error' paraphrases FTC Docs ('the OpMode rejects them during initialization'). The exact error behaviour was not observed.
'Four mecanum wheels are one of the most popular drivetrains in FTC' paraphrases gm0's 'very popular'. There is no usage data behind it.

pages.summary: Your first autonomous, an original lesson. By time: AutoByTime.java (LinearOpMode with setDrivePower and sleep), why it's unreliable (battery charge, floor slip), how RobotAutoDriveByTime_Linear uses an ElapsedTime loop instead, and a tip on @Autonomous(preselectTeleOp = ...) (verified in the Javadoc). By encoder: ticks per revolution (537.7 for a goBILDA 312 RPM Yellow Jacket, from RobotAutoDriveByGyro_Linear), gear reduction, wheel diameter, a worked figure of 42.8 ticks/in, and the reminder to set the motor type in the configuration. A RunMode table, then the five-step order drilled as a list: STOP_AND_RESET_ENCODER in INIT, setTargetPosition first, then RUN_TO_POSITION, unsigned setPower, wait on isBusy with a timeout. Wide two-file window: AutoByEncoder.java with numbered comments matching the steps, plus AutoByTime.java. Notes on ElapsedTime and the &&/|| isBusy choice (matching the SDK sample). IMU turns: a proportional controller with the error normalised to -180..180 and a worked -170 to 170 example. Wide window: AutoWithTurns.java uses hl_lines to highlight what's new against AutoByEncoder (IMU setup, resetYaw after PLAY, turnToHeading, headingError, getHeading, setDrivePower). Notes on how resetYaw carries over to teleop and on tuning TURN_KP. 'Why blocking code stops working' uses the example of an intake that must stop at 1.5 s while driving. 'State machines': enum, state field, switch in an iterative OpMode's loop(), ElapsedTime instead of sleep. Wide window: StateMachineAuto.java (enum Step {DRIVE_FORWARD, PAUSE, TURN_LEFT, DONE}, non-blocking startDrive/driveBusy/stopDrive, and a parallel intake timer). Then a 'The first seconds, loop by loop' walkthrough, gm0's warning against one giant switch for a purely step-by-step auto, and a 'Toward command-based' section linking linear-to-command-based.md (Commands.sequence/parallel replace the enum and switch). 'Try it': measure time vs encoder repeatability, and add a DRIVE_AGAIN state, with a checkpoint. Learn more links the three SDK auto samples, gm0 Encoders and FSM, FTC Docs Motor Modes and Encoders and the Universal IMU Interface, and the next page. One TODO diagram comment (state diagram).
uncertain: The code compiles, but nothing was run on a robot. The gains (TURN_KP 0.02, MAX_TURN 0.4, 2-degree tolerance) and the timeouts are starting points taken from the SDK gyro sample. The turn may stall short of the target on some robots, and the page tells students to tune it.
The claim that turns by encoder are less exact than IMU turns because of wheel slip is general robotics knowledge, not from a cited source.
The state machine reads isBusy() in the loop() call right after start() sets RUN_TO_POSITION. The SDK encoder sample relies on the same immediate isBusy() check, but I didn't test it on hardware.
4.0-inch wheels in TICKS_PER_INCH is the SDK sample's illustrative value, not a specific product.

The TURN_KP 0.02 / MAX_TURN 0.4 / 2-degree tolerance values come from the SDK gyro sample and may stall short of the target on some robots. The page tells students to tune them.

The claims that heading carries from auto into teleop and that teleop's imu.initialize() doesn't reset yaw rest on FTC Docs ('Heading is preserved between OpMode runs, unless the robot or RC app are restarted'). FTC Docs doesn't say directly whether initialize() resets yaw.

Two behaviours were checked against OpenFTC/Extracted-RC's OpModeManagerImpl, which is an older SDK extraction, not 12.0 source: 'the motors turn off' at STOP (callActiveOpModeStop puts every REV hub in failsafe and blocks hardware access) and object creation at INIT. They are very likely unchanged in 12.0 but weren't confirmed in 12.0 source. The writer's other uncertain points are now confirmed: motors default to FORWARD (HardwareDevice.resetDeviceConfigurationForOpMode Javadoc), the separate Autonomous list (REV docs), and invalid logo/USB pairs causing an exception at initialization (FTC Docs IMU page).

remaining_doubts.doubt: All eight Java files from the code windows, plus a snippets file for every short block outside them, compiled cleanly with javac 1.8 (-proc:none). They were compiled against the released RobotCore and Hardware 12.0.0 (BuildConfig says 12.0.0), Vision 12.0.0, SolversLib core and pedroPathing 0.3.6, Pedro core and revhub 3.0.2, and android.jar. Nothing was run on a robot. Panels @Configurable on a SubsystemBase subclass (Lift) is still not verified; only plain classes were checked.

'Set the target before the mode: the other way round gives an error' comes from gm0 (and matches first-autonomous.md). Since SDK 10.2 the exact behaviour is a logged stack trace, not a crash. I left it as is.

With the example gains, a target change gives a one-loop derivative kick (error jumps 0 to 1500). The power is clipped to ±1 and P already saturates, so it's harmless, but the page doesn't mention it.

SolversLib pedroPathing 0.3.6 declares Pedro revhub 3.0.0. I checked with javap that every Pedro member FollowPathCommand calls (Follower.follow/isBusy/following/holding/hold/stop/pose/algorithm/holdEnd, Path.with, ConfigVar.at, ForesightConfig.maxPathSpeed) exists with the same signature in 3.0.2. The combined Gradle setup itself was not build-tested.
The Discord size (over 4,000) and the Pedro release months come from the research notes (Discord invite count, Maven listing), not re-fetched today.

The Pinpoint heading sign is still not stated, and the spin push test doesn't need it. These were verified on hardware-free sources only: REV Color Sensor V3 implements DistanceSensor (javap) and HardwareMap.get uses isInstance; the AprilTag fields (javap on Vision 12.0.0); the clusters tech tip (R/B prefix, |roll| < 90, 4 clusters, no singles); the IMU page (BHI260AP from Sept 2022, default name 'imu', ±180 range, reset yaw only when level).
